Qurbonov, Behzod Bahodir ugli Davlatov, Alisher Baxtiyorovich Uzoqov, Lochinbek Mamurjon ugli Unplanned mechanical equipment failures are among the major sources of production losses and safety risks in the mining industry. Consequently, reliable prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) is a central task in predictive maintenance. Existing RUL models are generally specialized for a single equipment type and trained on laboratory datasets, which limits their transferability to mining equipment operating at temperatures of 45–60 °C and under variable loads of ±30 % due to domain shift. This article develops a unified learning architecture based on physics-informed machine learning and transfer learning (PIML+TL), integrated with unsupervised domain adaptation. The proposed framework encompasses three degradation mechanisms—bearings, gear transmissions, and hydraulic pumps—within a single model. Analytical expressions for RUL are derived from the Paris–Erdogan, Palmgren–Miner, and Arrhenius equations. A physics-enriched feature vector is constructed, and explicit formulations of the physics-based constraint terms are provided for each degradation mechanism. Statistical distribution shifts between laboratory and mining environments are addressed using the CORAL covariance alignment method, while the temperature-dependent component is incorporated through the Arrhenius acceleration factor. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the development of a unified neural network architecture capable of modeling multiple degradation mechanisms and a physics-constrained loss function whose physical terms are computed using unlabeled target-domain data. The study is theoretical and methodological in nature; experimental validation of the proposed methodology using real sensor data from mining enterprises is identified as a subsequent research stage. The data files are provided in JSON or JSON Lines format. Files Conversation records conversations-08-2025.jsonl — JSON Lines file containing 372 conversation records. Each line is a JSON object with conversation metadata and fields such as _id, userEmail, assistantId, timestamps, lastthreadrun, usage, and messages. example.json — A single example conversation record with the same structure as the records in conversations-08-2025.jsonl. Its messages and usage arrays are empty, so it illustrates the record format without including conversation content. Puzzle question-and-answer records puzzle1.json — 82 puzzle records. puzzle2.json — 81 puzzle records. puzzle3.json — 79 puzzle records. Each file contains nested arrays of question-and-answer objects. These objects include question and question_created_at; answer fields (answer and answer_created_at) may be absent when no answer is recorded. Puzzle user and conversation identifiers puzzle1_users.json — 82 records associated with Puzzle 1. puzzle2_users.json — 81 records associated with Puzzle 2. puzzle3_users.json — 79 records associated with Puzzle 3. Each record contains assistantId, conversationId, index, and userId, which can be used to associate identifiers with the corresponding puzzle data.
